codeReview.summary: The commit correctly renamed `lore.py` to `catalog_data.py` and the eight `world_web/daimoi_*.py` modules, but it did not complete the promised daimoi→particle rename across the full Python backend. Functional scripts under `part64/scripts/` still contain stale daimoi imports, symbols, and payload keys, so VAL-BR-002 is not satisfied.

issues.description: This script still imports `code.world_web.daimoi_probabilistic` and calls `build_probabilistic_daimoi_particles` / `reset_probabilistic_daimoi_state_for_tests` even though the feature renamed that module to `particle_probabilistic.py`. The rename was therefore not propagated to all backend Python code, and this helper script is left broken.

Backend scripts still expose daimoi-named runtime fields and payload keys such as `daimoi_backend`, `daimoi_backend_error`, `embed_daimoi`, and `daimoi_probabilistic`. Equivalent stale references also remain in `part64/scripts/eval_sim_learning_suite.py:236` and `part64/scripts/homeostasis_soak_probe.py:397`, so the backend-wide rename required by the feature/VAL-BR-002 is incomplete.

blockingIssues.description: Stale imports still target the removed `code.world_web.daimoi_probabilistic` module, leaving this backend script inconsistent with the rename and breaking the promise to update all old module references.

Functional Python scripts outside `part64/code/` still use daimoi-named fields and request keys (`daimoi_backend`, `embed_daimoi`, `daimoi_probabilistic`), so the daimoi→particle rename was not completed throughout the Python backend.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Backend rename work is currently scoped/documented too narrowly around `part64/code`, which makes it easy to miss functional Python scripts in `part64/scripts/` during search and verification.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `AGENTS.md:27-29` maps `part64/code` but does not mention `part64/scripts/`; the worker transcript/handoff verified `rg 'daimoi|daimon' part64/code/ --type py -l`; yet `git grep -n -i "daimo" 99dee817b01aa4f0e325b7136a5e60eaf563bb3d -- "*.py"` still finds multiple stale refs in `part64/scripts/*.py`.

sharedStateObservations.observation: `VAL-BR-002a` is broader than this feature slice: the feature claims it fulfills that assertion, but the commit still contains other narrative-named `world_web` modules that were only renamed by the later `rename-narrative-modules` feature.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: `features.json:490-493` maps `rename-core-data-model` to `VAL-BR-002a`; `validation-contract.md:43-45` defines VAL-BR-002a as renaming all narrative-named `world_web` modules including `muse_runtime.py`; `git ls-tree --name-only -r 99dee817b01aa4f0e325b7136a5e60eaf563bb3d part64/code/world_web | rg '(muse_runtime|nooi|lith_ecs)\.py|particle_.*\.py'` still lists `muse_runtime.py`, `nooi.py`, and `lith_ecs.py` in that commit.

commands.observation: Confirmed the intended renames landed in 34 files, including `part64/code/lore.py -> catalog_data.py` and eight `world_web/daimoi_*.py -> particle_*.py` renames.

Found residual daimoi/daimon references in functional Python scripts under `part64/scripts/`, including a stale import from `code.world_web.daimoi_probabilistic` and several daimoi-named payload keys/fields.
Showed that the commit mixed renamed particle modules with still-narrative `muse_runtime.py`, `nooi.py`, and `lith_ecs.py`, which is relevant to the over-broad VAL-BR-002a mapping.

summary: Fail: the feature completed the core module/file renames inside `part64/code`, but it left broken and stale daimoi references in backend Python scripts under `part64/scripts/`, so the claimed backend-wide rename/VAL-BR-002 is not fully satisfied.
